html:
The Netherlands Indies was the Dutch colony that became Indonesia. The Dutch state took it over in 1800 from the bankrupt Dutch East India Company. The map shows it from 1880 to 1914; the colony as a whole is also under Dutch East Indies.

From 1830 to 1870 the Cultivation System forced Javanese villages to grow coffee, sugar and indigo for export, which made the Netherlands rich. After 1870 private plantations took over: tobacco and rubber in Sumatra, sugar in Java. Oil was found in Sumatra, and Royal Dutch Petroleum was founded in 1890 to pump it.

The years on the map were a time of conquest. The Dutch fought the long Aceh War from 1873, took Bali in bloody campaigns in 1906 and 1908, and by the 1910s held the whole archipelago. The Krakatoa eruption of 1883 killed some 36,000 people.

From 1901 an "Ethical Policy" promised schools and welfare. A new educated class grew, including the writer Kartini, and the first national movements began, among them Muhammadiyah in 1912. Japan occupied the colony in 1942, and Indonesia declared independence in 1945.
